subject: Northwind Retail - Incident escalation: remediation plan and exec readout
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@northwindretail.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Northwind SRE <sre-team@northwindretail.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Increased latency & error rate impacting checkout - immediate exec attention requested

Michael / Redwood team,

We experienced a sustained degradation on our inference-backed checkout widgets this morning between 07:45-08:25 PDT. Symptoms: 3x median latency, tail latency spiking to ~6s, and an increased error rate (5-8%) across /v1/generate on our production model routes. Throughput appeared to drop as well; customers saw timeouts. This impacted ~18% of our checkouts during the window and is causing material revenue impact.

Please escalate — our CTO is asking for a short executive readout and an RCA delivered to us by EOD Monday. We need:
- Temporary mitigations to restore performance now (capacity, fallbacks)
- A technical root cause summary and corrective actions
- A timeline for permanent fixes and an ask about SLA credits for the incident window

I've attached a short incident summary from our end (incident_summary_nw_20270612.pdf). We can join a bridge immediately if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Director of Engineering, Northwind Retail

[attachment: incident_summary_nw_20270612.pdf]

- We will provide an interim technical memo within 2 hours and a draft RCA by EOD Monday (PST).
- Schedule an exec readout with me and our Head of Product Ops — please share a 30‑minute slot that works for your CTO and execs.

Looping in the bridge notes and an action breakdown. Teams are on it — snapshot below (I'll update the sheet).

Short findings so far (preliminary):
- Autoscaler hit an unexpected soft cap on slot allocation for northwind-prod, which prevented timely scale-up under a traffic spike.
- A queued kernel update we rolled out last night appears to be selecting a less efficient matmul path under certain batch-size distributions; that increased p99 latencies on a subset of nodes.
- Several requests fell back to an alternate model variant with cold KV cache entries — increased compute and elevated error rates.

Immediate actions (owners):
- Rishi: validate kernel selection regression, identify safe revert. (ETA 3 hours)
- Kim: temporarily increase slot limit for northwind-prod and add emergency capacity. (ETA 30 minutes)
- Marissa: prep customer-facing incident summary for Elena. (ETA 1 hour)
- Grace: draft exec readout slides and timeline. (ETA EOD Monday for full draft)

Attaching draft RCA doc we’ll iterate on. Sharing the action tracker: action_tracker_sheet.xlsx.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Increased latency & error rate impacting checkout - immediate exec attention requested

Quick technical summary (preliminary root cause):
1) Autoscaler soft cap: our configured "slot_limit" for the northwind-prod pool was lower than anticipated after the last policy change; during the traffic spike the autoscaler did not add sufficient instances, leading to queueing and higher backend latency.
2) Kernel selection regression: the nightly kernel selector prioritized a quantized matmul path that shows worse performance for short sequences / small batch sizes typical of checkout requests. On impacted nodes this increased p99 by ~1.5-2s.
3) Model variant fallback & KV cache coldness: some traffic hit a fallback variant (smaller memory config) which had a cold KV cache and produced extra backend work and occasional OOMs — those requests surfaced as 5xx.

Proposed mitigations (short-term):
- Revert kernel selector change for the fleet and monitor (Rishi).
- Temporarily lift slot_limit for northwind-prod to allow faster scale-up (Kim).
- Preload KV caches for the primary model variant during the mitigation window.
- Add an emergency routing rule to preferentially route traffic to nodes with warm caches and stable kernel path.

I ran heapdump snippets and logs; attaching a small excerpt. I estimate a 60–90 minute window to verify the revert and confirm reductions in error rate and tail latency.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

[attachment: heapdump_snippet.txt]

- Temporary capacity uplift applied to northwind-prod pool on Jun 12; slot_limit increased and emergency routing installed. Observed error rate drop from ~6% to <0.5% and p99 tail reductions within 90 minutes of mitigations.
- Kernel selector revert completed on Jun 12 for the affected fleet subset; validated performance regressions resolved.
- Preload job run to warm KV caches for the principal variant.

Open deliverables and timeline:
- Final RCA document (PDF + slides) — delivering by EOD Monday, Jun 21. [attached: postincident_rca_final_v1.pdf will be added to the doc link]
- Permanent fixes: ship autoscaler policy adjustment + improved canary for kernel selector + mandatory KV prewarm on model rollout. Planned ship date: July 6, 2027.
- SLA credit: we will submit a formal credit proposal to finance this week; preliminary estimate ~8–12% prorated for the impacted window pending legal/finance approval.

Action tracker (live): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cRcaDraftDoc — I updated owners and ETA columns.

Owners recap:
- Rishi: finalize kernel selector canary and revert guardrails (ETA 2027-06-25)
- Kim: autoscaler policy change and monitoring alerts (ETA 2027-06-28)
- Marissa: customer-facing summary and credit conversation owner (ongoing)
- Grace: post-incident exec brief + followup cadence (ongoing)

We’ll keep the bridge open for the next 72 hours for any regressions and provide weekly progress updates until ship. Thanks again for the partnership and patience — we’re committed to preventing recurrence.

Michael Grant
